description: The smallest step of the world clock. Everything that happens in the world is paced by it; one tick is thirty-six seconds of world time, and a world day is 2,400 ticks.
The fixed sequence of phases the world runs through on every tick, from choosing who acts to saving the result. It is the same every time, so a world replays identically from the same start.
Within a tick, entities are handled in a fixed order, so the same starting state and seed always give the same outcome.
A decision is made once and then carried through over the following ticks, instead of being rethought every tick.
Anything that lives in the world and can act or be acted on, such as a hero, a monster or a townsperson. Each has attributes, a faction and a position.
The core numbers that describe what an entity is naturally good at. Health, damage and speed are worked out from them.
An entity's basic calling, such as Novice, Warrior, Mage or Rogue. It sets the starting strength and the gear an entity begins with.
How far an entity has grown through experience. Each level earns attribute points and can unlock new skills.
What an entity earns by acting, chiefly by defeating foes, and spends to gain levels. Each level needs more than the one before.
Hunger, sleep and exhaustion, which build up as time passes and must be met by eating, resting and recovering. Going without them wears an entity down and can kill it.
Lasting damage from a single very heavy hit that the entity survives. It weakens the entity's fighting strength and health, and today a wound does not heal.
A lasting mark meant to replace a wound as it fades, with a smaller penalty. Not yet in play: no scars form today.
The side an entity belongs to: the hero guild, the monster horde, the town council, or neutral. Factions hold relations with one another and can claim regions.
What a successful attack takes from the target's health. It depends on the attacker's strength, the defender's toughness and the way the fight is being fought.
How ready an entity is to act. An attack can only be made once readiness is full, so fighters strike in turn rather than every tick.
The state of two or more fighters being locked in melee. An engaged fighter who wants to leave must make a decision to do so, and that decision may cost it a free swing.
The extra blow an engaged hostile gets when its opponent disengages. A fighter that knows such a swing would kill it does not flee. Also called an opportunity attack.
Reaching zero health ends an entity, whatever its role; no one is exempt. The cause of death is recorded.
How worn a piece of equipment is. It wears down with fighting, and broken equipment gives no bonus at all.
The extra time it takes to cross difficult ground, so a road is quicker than a swamp.
Goods and gold are never created or lost in a transfer. Whatever leaves one holder arrives at another in the same step, or nothing moves at all.
What an entity carries, limited by slots and weight. A full pack cannot take more.
A place in the world where materials can be gathered, such as an ore vein or a berry thicket. It holds a limited supply and runs out.
How depleted resource nodes come back after a wait, so the land is not stripped bare for good.
Where entities buy from and sell to shops. Prices depend on the item and on the buyer's standing.
A region owner's shared purse, paid into by a share of sales and wages in its lands and drawn on for upkeep.
Turning gathered materials into new goods at a workplace, under the same rule that nothing appears from nowhere.
A private store at an entity's home that only its owner can use, and only while standing there.
What an entity is trying to get done. Entities weigh their concerns and take up the most pressing one, with survival first, then bodily needs, then social ties, then wealth.
The concrete piece of work an entity is currently pursuing, broken down into steps. Others may take its place if something more pressing arises.
A remembered piece of information about a place or resource, such as where ore was seen. Its certainty fades if it is not refreshed.
A remembered reason a goal cannot be reached, such as a blocked path, missing materials or a full pack.
How strongly an entity sticks to what it is doing, so it drops a task for something else only when the new thing is clearly more pressing.
A kind of outing an entity can choose, such as gathering, hunting or a quest, scored by what it is likely to gain against the danger.
A bounded area of the world with its own terrain, danger and ownership. Deaths and events are credited to the region they happen in.
A region's record of recent violence. Violent deaths raise it; it drives hazards and can set off larger threats. In current worlds it stays low.
A standing danger in a region that wears entities down just by being there, draining health and adding to their tiredness.
Which faction holds a region. Influence shifts when entities die there, and past a threshold the region changes hands.
A region's balance of power between factions. It moves with deaths in the region.
A large world threat that can arise when a world has grown mature and a region has taken enough trauma, such as raids or powerful bosses. Boss spawns are switched off today.
The slow turnover of a region's population as people are born, age and die. It runs on a long, fixed interval. In current worlds it produces no births or deaths yet.
A formal arrangement between two entities, such as hiring, a loan, a lesson or a team-up.

A contract by which one entity asks another to join it and follow its lead. By the law it is weighed on trust, the other's social state and pay; in play today an offer is accepted without that weighing.
How willing one entity is to believe and work with another, built from history, bonds and standing. By the law it decides whether contracts are accepted.
A lasting tie between two entities, such as friendship or grievance, that grows or fades with what happens between them.
An entity's general standing with others. It raises trust, earns shop discounts and passes down to heirs.
A group of entities moving and fighting together. It has a gathering point, roles for its members, and a leader, who gives way to a clearly more sociable member.
How closely a party's members stay together around its gathering point.
A hero organisation with a hall that entities can visit. Guild ranks and dues are not yet in play.
